title: Two real men were doing it
learning_goal: Know that Thomas Cook and George Francis Train really went round the world just as Verne wrote; feel that Fogg's bet was in the air.

narration.script: Two real men: one travelling as Verne wrote, the other already home. Thomas Cook left Liverpool in late September 1872, going west — the first commercial round-the-world tour. It took him two hundred and twenty-two days. He was mid-ocean when Fogg's story began. George Francis Train had reached home earlier — on the twenty-first of December 1870. Fogg's date, two years early. He later claimed, 'Verne stole my thunder. I'm Phileas Fogg.'
